caseno:
First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 193 of 1994
with
Civil Rule No.264 (FM)of 1994
lawyer:
Sasanka Sekhar Sarker. Advocate for SS Haider, Senior Advocate— For the Appellants
Miah Abdul Gafur with Ataur Rahman Khan, Advocates — For the Respondents
parties:
Tara Miah and another ------ Appellants
Vs.
Shahjada Sarder and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha J: This appeal is directed against the order dated 17-7-94 passed by the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No.41 of 1993 (Partition) rejecting the plaintiff''s prayer for temporary injunction under Order 39 rules 1 and 2 CPC.

2. The appellants as plaintiffs filed the aforesaid suit for partition claiming 10 decimals of land in their share out of 2.37 1/2 acres of land consisting of a tank, a dwelling house and naal land. After filing the suit the plaintiffs filed the application for temporary injunction praying for restraining the defendants from making any construction in suit plot No 86 only and from changing the nature and character of suit land.

3. Defendant Nos. 8 and 9, 11-15 opposed the application for injunction contending, inter anti, that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land. It has been further contended in the written objection that defendant Nos. 9-15 have title and possession over 3 decimals of land in suit plot No. 86 in which their homestead stands and the said land has also been duly recorded in their names in the RS Khatian and they have been paying rent regularly to the appropriate authority. It has been further contended that defendant No. 9 has already constructed a pucca building in suit plot No. 86 and there are other structures standing thereon and the said land is well fenced by walls on all four sides and under such circumstances there is absolutely no ground for granting temporary injunction on vague and indefinite assertions of the plaintiffs.

<u>4. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dated 17-7-94 found that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a prima facie case in support of their claim for temporary injunction. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the materials on record also found that there is nothing on record to prima facie prove that the plaintiffs have possession in suit plot No. 86. On the other hand, the constesting defendants have produced the certified copies of the finally published RS Khatian in which 26 decimals of land has been recorded in their names. From the DCR and the rent receipts produced by the contesting defendant if is found that they have been paying rent to the appropriate authority for the said land. RAJUK has already approved their plan for construction of buildings in the said land. It has been clearly asserted in the written objection that the construction of the building has already been finished. Suit plot No. 86 admittedly measures 32 decimals of land in which the contesting defendants appear to have possession over 20 decimals of land. The plaintiffs alleged claim of 10 decimals of land in this particular part is totally vague and indefinite. In such circumstances, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a prima facie case for injunction. From the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record we find that the learned Subordinate Judge was perfectly justified in refusing the plaintiffs'' prayer for temporary injunction. We find no illegality in the impugned order calling for our interference.</u>

<u>5. The principle of relating to the grant of temporary injunction against co-sharers is well-settled by now. Ordinarily a co-sharer is entitled to possess every inch of the joint property but when a co-sharer is found to be in exclusive possession over a specific portion of the joint property he is entitled under the law to protect his possession against the inroads of his co-sharers by way of injunction until the joint property is partitioned by metes and bounds. But in this case we find nothing on record to show that the plaintiffs have possession in suit plot No. 86 not to speak of exclusive possession. In that view of the matter the appeal is found to be without any substance and, as such, it is liable to be dismissed.</u>

6. In the result, the appeal is dismissed and the connected Rule being Civil Rule No. 264 (FM) of 1994 is discharged. There shall be no order as to costs.

The order of maintaining status quo is hereby vacated.

End.
